findings.symbol: TC-02-INT-06, the step and expected result added for the immutability-before-uniqueness ordering
findings.claim: The ordering rule the repair added — a topic write answers the audience or kind immutability violation before the name-uniqueness one — is observed by a call that cannot fail if the ordering is implemented backwards. The step sends `audience: "client"` on a staff topic together with a name another seeded staff topic holds, and uniqueness is per organization and audience. An implementation that checks uniqueness first against the audience the body asks for finds no client topic holding that name, falls through and answers the same `400` `audienceImmutable`; only an implementation that checks uniqueness first against the stored audience answers `409`. The contracts sentence leaves the same gap: 'a name another topic of that audience already holds' does not say whether 'that audience' is the stored one or the one the body sent, and the two readings disagree about whether a duplicate exists at all. The prescribed answer is the same under both readings, so no implementation is materially different and this is not an ambiguity that blocks — but the case bought to pin the ordering pins it against one of the two backwards implementations only.

witness.detail: Seeded staff topics include Claude; seeded client topics are Access and Other (contracts, Seed Data). PATCH a staff topic with { audience: 'client', name: 'Claude' }. Reading A, uniqueness evaluated on the requested audience 'client': no client topic is named Claude, so no 409 exists to be answered first and the case passes even with uniqueness checked before immutability. Reading B, uniqueness evaluated on the stored audience 'staff': Claude is taken, so uniqueness-first answers 409 and the case fails. The name `Other` is seeded in both audiences and would be a duplicate under either reading.
witness.source: specs/requests/02-request-topics.cases.md:243 and :249 against specs/requests/02-request-topics.contracts.md:304 and the Seed Data table at :265-276

findings.suggestedFix: Send the duplicate as `Other`, which the seed holds in both audiences, so the 409 exists under either reading of the uniqueness scope; and say in the contracts sentence which audience's names the uniqueness check considers on a write that also asks to change the audience.
